classification: SYNTHETIC NONPROD ACCEPTANCE FIXTURE. The reusable persona end-to-end scenario layer over the Sample Company persona catalog. Contains no credential, no password, no token, no connection string and no production identity.

basis.$comment: Every persona key, Employee id and capability key named here is DECLARED there or in sampleCompany.v2.json. This manifest declares no persona, no Employee, no Principal, no Security Role, no Work Eligibility and no Operational Scope of its own. It declares SCENARIOS and the measured truth about whether each one can run.

readinessMeaning.READY: Every authority, route, grant and fixture row the scenario needs EXISTS in nonprod today and has been measured. The only remaining per-run step is activating the persona's sandbox password through the existing governed credential path, which is an operator action and not a platform gap.
readinessMeaning.PARTIAL: The authority exists and is measurable, but some part of the scenario -- a route, a record, a grant row -- does not. The blocker is named.
readinessMeaning.BLOCKED: The scenario cannot run at all today. The blocker is named.
readinessMeaning.BLOCKED_PENDING_C5: Blocked specifically because the Commercial record families hold zero rows after the authorized cleanup, and the 12 deleted synthetic Commercial records must NOT be recreated. Never merged into plain BLOCKED and never faked.

clientSurface.$comment: Q7 asks for login, landing/North Star, navigation visibility, record visibility, allowed and denied actions. Three of those six are decided by the client, and the client does not read EOS authority to decide them. That is the single most important measurement in this manifest.

clientSurface.landingPage: ONE constant for everybody: '/' redirects to /dashboard (App.jsx:865) and the catch-all does the same (App.jsx:1144). There is no per-persona landing redirect. The only branch is DashboardIndex -> TechnicianDashboard when role === 'technician', otherwise MyDashboard (App.jsx:226-235).
clientSurface.northStarIsNotALandingPage: CORRECTION TO THE BRIEF'S WORDING. In this repository 'North Star' is a per-surface design and acceptance STANDARD, enforced by per-domain Playwright quick gates (dispatchNorthStarQuickGate.mjs, equipmentNorthStarQuickGate.mjs, financialsNorthStarQuickGate.mjs, partsNorthStarQuickGate.mjs, receivingNorthStarQuickGate.mjs, serviceOperationsNorthStarGate.mjs) and by domain modules such as src/domain/accountNorthStar.js. It is not a page a persona lands on. A scenario that asserts 'persona X lands on its North Star' would be asserting something the product does not have.

navigationVisibilityAuthority.consequenceForThisCatalog: GOVERNED_PERSONA_HAS_NO_CLIENT_ROLE. The 15 governed personas hold PostgreSQL Security Roles (partsAssociate, warehouseManager, purchasingManager, salesperson, fieldManager, ...). The client's navigation mechanism cannot read any of them; it reads a Firestore users/{uid}.role that is one of three values, and the Sample Company login-activation phase writes NO Firestore document. A governed persona can therefore AUTHENTICATE and call the EOS API, and cannot navigate the client, because navigation authority and business authority are two different systems today.

canonicalPersonas.notes: Holds `owner` and NOT `admin`. Measured nonprod 2026-09-24: `owner` carries 47 granted capabilities, `admin` carries 66, `owner` is a STRICT SUBSET and 19 capabilities are admin-only. The previous note here said this persona 'holds the `admin` Role key, which is what the Administration mutation surface actually checks' -- which was true of the merged fixture and was exactly the merge the Owner ruled out.
canonicalPersonas.whatMakesItDifferent: Administration's definition surface -- editObjectDefinition, editRoleDefinition, editWorkflowDefinition -- is gated on the Role KEY `admin` and nothing else, so this persona is REFUSED all three while still holding admin.employeeWorkEligibility.write and admin.employeeOperationalScope.write, which are capability-gated and which `owner` does hold. assignRole permits owner | generalManager | admin, so it keeps that one. That is a measurable, three-way difference from both the Administrator and the General Manager.
canonicalPersonas.principalDisposition: ADOPTS the `owner`-holding Principal that ALREADY EXISTS in nonprod and had NO Employee link at all -- which is why every WORK_ELIGIBILITY / OPERATIONAL_SCOPE / RECORD_ASSIGNMENT predicate refused it EMPLOYEE_LINK_REQUIRED. No Principal is created, no credential is created, reset or rotated.
canonicalPersonas.authorityNotWidened: The `owner` Role is WITHHELD from the Sample Company's capability-grant reconciliation. The compiled catalog declares `owner` identically to `admin`, so reconciling it would add the nineteen admin-only capabilities to the live Owner Role -- the one way the Owner ruled this asymmetry may NOT be closed.

canonicalPersonas.notes: Holds `admin`, through the ONE reused real sandbox administrator Principal -- never recreated, never renamed, never re-credentialed. Sample Company v1 linked that Principal to the Owner / Executive Employee; v2 links it to this one.

canonicalPersonas.whyTheMergeWasWrong: The merge evidence argued that a second Principal holding `admin` would answer identically on all 19 mutations and all 13 reads. That is true and was never the question: Owner and Administrator do not hold the same Role. The merged fixture concealed that by giving the Owner / Executive persona the ADMINISTRATOR's Role, so the two 'identical' personas were identical by construction.
canonicalPersonas.correctsAMeasurablyFalseClaim: The merge also recorded that a persona holding `owner` but not `admin` 'is the genuinely missing administrative persona' and that 'the catalog contains no such persona'. MEASURABLY FALSE: a Principal holding `owner` and not `admin` exists in nonprod today, with 47 granted capabilities. It had no Employee link, which is why nothing could reach it -- not because it did not exist. The Owner / Executive persona now adopts it.

$canonicalPersonas_comment: SEVENTEEN DISPOSITIONED ROWS FOR THE OWNER'S SIXTEEN-PERSONA POPULATION. The sixteen the Owner named are Owner/Executive, Administrator, General Manager, Service Manager, Dispatcher, Technician (assigned), Technician (unassigned), Parts Associate, Parts Manager/Purchasing, Warehouse Associate, Warehouse Manager, Retail Sales, National Accounts Sales, Finance/Accounting, Reporting (BLOCKED_DOMAIN) and Restricted. The seventeenth row is 'Purchasing', kept as an explicit MERGED disposition into parts-manager because the Owner's own population writes that persona as 'Parts Manager/Purchasing' -- the merge is recorded rather than silently absorbed, so what would separate the two again stays written down. The previous list held fourteen rows and was wrong in four ways: Administrator was MERGED into Owner/Executive, Service Manager was not dispositioned at all, the two technicians were one row with the unassigned one demoted to a `variant`, and Restricted did not exist.
